data.title: Asante Reports Q3 2026 Operating & Financial Results and Issues Clarification Regarding November 12, 2026 Press Release
data.description:
HIGHLIGHTS

  • Q3 2026 gold production of 48,517 equivalent ounces at a consolidated AISC of $4,860 per ounce; nine month 2026 gold production of 165,594 equivalent ounces, up 41.0% year-on-year, at a consolidated AISC of $4,308 per ounce.
  • Chirano delivered improved quarterly production of 34,420 gold equivalent ounces, up 34.4% year-on-year, primarily driven by higher-grade ore from Aboduabo.
  • Bibiani production was impacted by operational challenges, including reduced availability of the principal mining contractor in the Main Pit, lower plant recovery, power disruptions and slower than anticipated resettlement. As a result, 2026 production and AISC guidance has been withdrawn. A second contractor has been onboarded to expedite waste clearance from the January 2026 south-east wall failure in the Main Pit. This is expected to be completed in early December 2026, allowing renewed ore access in that area by Q1 2027.
  • Nine month 2026 revenue of $756.7 million, up 103.3% year-on-year, driven by a 40.2% increase in average realized gold price together with a 45.1% increase in gold equivalent ounces sold.
  • Adjusted EBITDA increased to $194.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $0.6 million for the prior year comparable period, and $34.7 million for Q3 2026.
  • Strong initial drill results were returned from the Bibiani Bridge area between the Main Pit and Cut 5, including 60m at 3.13 Au(g/t) from 103m in hole MGRC26-763, 48m at 2.12 g/t Au from 42m, 25m at 4.95 g/t Au from 119m and 6m at 62.48 g/t Au from 136m, supporting the potential to extend open-pit mining (refer to separate 13 Nov. press release).
  • Expanding the Main Pit to include the Bibiani Bridge would potentially enable portions of the existing northern Main Pit underground Mineral Resource to be accessed from surface and thereby reallocated into the open-pit LOM plan. In turn, this would allow the deferral of significant underground development capital expenditure currently planned for 2027 and 2028. Management plans to accelerate drilling, assaying, and mine planning in this area with results to be incorporated into an updated Main Pit Mineral Resource model and revised mine plan.

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Asante Gold Corporation (TSXV: ASE | GSE: ASG | OTCQX: ASGOF) ("Asante" or the "Company") reports its operating and financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, with highlights provided in Table 1 below. This press release is a clarification to, and replaces in its entirety, the press release dated November 12, 2026 that was issued by a news service without the Company's authorization. Although the financial information in this press release is substantially and materially similar to the financial information in the November 12, 2026 press release, readers are advised to disregard the November 12, 2026 press release. All dollar figures are in United States dollars unless otherwise indicated. Following the change in the Company's financial year end to December 31, comparative figures are for the three and nine months ended October 31, 2025.

Campbell Baird, Acting Chief Executive Officer of Asante, commented:

“We continue to make progress in resetting the business, although there is still considerable work ahead of us. Our priority remains on improving operational performance across both mines and establishing a more consistent and sustainable production base in order to realize the true organic potential of Chirano and Bibiani, which we believe to be substantial. We are in the process of finalizing a comprehensive operational turnaround plan, which diagnoses the individual drivers of the persistent underperformance of the assets, and which will define the corresponding remediation steps required for resolution. That plan is expected to set timelines for the achievement of remediation milestones and to quantify any related capital requirements. Asante expects to communicate the turnaround plan to the market in January 2027 once finalized.

Chirano delivered a stronger quarter, with production up 34% on the comparable quarter in 2025, and we continue to identify opportunities to improve productivity and efficiency. At Bibiani, production was impacted by a number of factors, including mining contractor equipment availability, power disruptions, lower plant recoveries, and resettlement delays, leading us to withdraw our 2026 production and cost guidance. We have since mobilized a second mining contractor to accelerate waste clearance in the southeast area of the Main Pit, with ore access expected to be restored from Q1 2027. In parallel, we are implementing measures to improve plant stability and power reliability, including additional backup generation capacity and automated restart capabilities, to support more consistent production.

At the same time, we’re encouraged by the initial drilling results at the Bibiani Bridge area, which are highlighting a significant opportunity to improve the mine plan that must be fast-tracked. An expanded Main Pit could allow us to access mineralization currently planned for underground mining and potentially defer significant development capital. This is an important example of our broader objective to maximise Asante’s organic potential, to boost capital efficiency and to unlock greater value from our operations.”

Operating Summary

Total material mined at Bibiani was 46.5 million tonnes for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 11.6% on the prior year comparable period, with mining rates increasing from Q4 2025 through the first five months of 2026. In Q3 2026, total material mined was 14.0 million tonnes, a decrease of 18.7% on the prior year comparable period, primarily due to reduced equipment availability of the principal mining contractor in the Main Pit, which slowed remediation of the Main Pit southeast wall and access to higher grade ore. Outstanding resettlement of Phase 1 households also restricted blasting and access to planned mining areas in the Main Pit. A second contractor has been onboarded to augment production, and the Walsh Pit is being backfilled to provide short haul opportunities.

Russel Pit was completed during Q3 2026, with 9,187 ounces of gold contained in ore mined during the quarter and 93,875 contained ounces mined over the life of the pit. Main Pit Cut 6, a satellite deposit north of the Main Pit, was also commissioned to maintain ore delivery, and Main Pit Cut 2 was re-engineered to absorb the waste movement deficit. Remediation of the Main Pit southeast wall is expected to be completed in early December 2026, supporting increased ore delivery in Q1 2027.

Gold equivalent production at Bibiani was 14,097 ounces in Q3 2026 and 65,835 ounces for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with 11,721 ounces and 37,220 ounces in the respective prior-year periods, reflecting increased ore throughput, higher plant feed grades and improved recoveries. Gold recovery averaged 57.6% in Q3 2026 and 70.7% for the nine-month period, compared with 55.9% and 63.2%, respectively, in the prior year. However, Q3 recovery declined from 75.2% in H1 2026, reflecting plant performance and stability issues, as well as power disruptions during the quarter.

An independent technical review of the Bibiani processing plant, completed by CrystalForge Technologies (CFT) in September 2026, identified the crushing and grinding circuit as the main constraint on plant performance. Following the removal of the original primary crusher from service, the plant has relied on mobile crushing units, which produce feed that does not meet the design specification of the SAG mill. This has prevented consistent grinding, which in turn has affected flotation and leach performance. A plant stability and reliability program is being implemented, and CFT’s work with the Company is ongoing. The Company expects to update the market on the plant remediation and recommissioning work recommended by CFT as part of its operational turnaround plan (see “2026 Outlook”).

AISC decreased to $7,681 per ounce for Q3 2026 and $4,994 per ounce for the nine months, from $8,776 per ounce and $6,464 per ounce, respectively, primarily due to higher gold equivalent ounces sold, partially offset by higher cost of sales and sustaining capital expenditures. AISC in Q3 2026 was higher than the $4,268 per ounce reported in H1 2026, reflecting lower ounces sold as plant feed grade and recovery declined.

The Company’s resettlement programme for the Bibiani Old Town and Zongo communities continued to progress during the period. Approximately $57 million has been invested in the programme to date, including the construction of a new school complex. Relocation of Phase 1 households to the new site commenced in late July 2026, with implementation advancing at a measured pace as the Company continues engaging closely with affected households. As at September 30, 2026, 457 of 846 Phase 1 households had been relocated, with the monthly rate increasing from 12 households in July to 201 households in August and 244 households in September. The Company is working with the remaining households with the aim of completing the Phase 1 relocation by the end of 2026.

Open pit ore mined at Chirano increased by 141.5% and 117.1% in Q3 2026 and the nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the prior year comparable periods, primarily driven by the ramp up of open pit activities at Aboduabo in early 2026, supported by an expanded contractor fleet. Underground ore mined decreased by 5.1% in Q3 2026, primarily due to fewer ore tonnes mined from Suraw, and increased by 2.2% for the nine months, primarily due to higher ore tonnes mined from Akoti and Tano.

Gold equivalent production at Chirano was 34,420 ounces for Q3 2026 and 99,759 ounces for the nine months, up from 25,612 ounces and 80,239 ounces in the prior year comparable periods, reflecting higher ore processed and higher grade, partially offset by a slightly lower recovery rate for the nine months due to a higher proportion of Aboduabo material in the blend. AISC increased to $3,722 per ounce for Q3 2026 and $3,836 per ounce for the nine months, from $2,964 per ounce and $2,673 per ounce, respectively, primarily due to higher royalties reflecting the Company’s revenue based royalty structure in Ghana combined with the higher average realized gold price, and higher sustaining capital expenditures, including underground development at Obra and Suraw, open pit stripping at Sariehu and the tailings storage facility embankment raise.

Key project milestones included completion of the crushing circuit upgrade, which became operational at the end of October 2026, replacement of the Mill 02 feed end half shell, installation of a carbon regeneration kiln with commissioning scheduled for November 2026, installation of CIL intertank screens and carbon advance pumps, and progress on the TSF1 southeast stage 2 raise, with Phase 1 approximately 95% complete as at September 2026.

Exploration

Exploration expenditure at Bibiani and Chirano totalled $4.5 million for Q3 2026 and $16.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, with 26,234 metres drilled during the quarter and 83,963 metres for the nine months.

Bibiani:

During Q3 2026, the Company completed a review of near mine exploration opportunities at Bibiani, identifying priority targets with the potential to support open pit extensions, including the Bridge area between the Main Pit and Cut 5, the gap between Cut 5 and Cut 6, and down dip extensions beneath Cut 5. An 8,000m reverse circulation and diamond drilling programme commenced during the period to test these targets, planned over approximately 350m of strike and to a depth of approximately 150m.

The Bridge hosts Inferred Mineral Resources and Indicated Mineral Resources, which are incorporated in the current underground mine design. With previous mine planning focused on underground development, the potential to access this mineralization through an expanded open pit had not been fully evaluated.

Subsequent to quarter end, initial results from infill drilling at the Bridge were received, supporting the continuity of mineralization between the Main Pit and Cut 5. Significant intercepts include including 60m at 3.13 Au(g/t) from 103m in hole MGRC26-763, 48m at 2.12 g/t Au from 42m in hole MGRC26‑741, which ended in mineralization at 90m; 25m at 4.95 g/t Au from 119m in MGRC26‑762B; 40m at 2.76 g/t Au from 65m in MGRC26‑743; 13m at 5.59 g/t Au from 85m and 60m at 3.13 g/t Au from 103m in MGRC26‑763; and 6m at 62.48 g/t Au from 136m in MGRC26‑765 (refer to news release, “Bridge Drilling Programme Results”, dated November 13, 2026).

The current Bibiani underground plan is based on the 2025 Definitive Feasibility Study, which favoured an earlier transition from open pit to underground mining beneath the Main Pit. The results received to date are supportive of an alternative scenario that would extend open pit operations between the existing pits, including access to parts of the northern Main Pit underground Mineral Resource from surface (refer to 13 November related press release).

Continued success from the Bibiani Bridge drill programme could increase open pit ore availability and extend surface operations, which could in turn result in the deferral of the underground development and related capital expenditure currently planned for 2027 and 2028. Any revision to the mine plan remains subject to the results of further drilling and technical and economic evaluation. No firm estimate of additional tonnes, grade, mine life extension has been made at this stage. The 8,000m drilling programme is expected to be completed in Q4 2026, and the results will be incorporated into an updated Main Pit Mineral Resource model and revised mine plan.

Chirano

Exploration continued during Q3 2026 at Obra North Extensions, Suraw, Sariehu UG and Mamnao North. At Mamnao North, mineralization has been extended laterally by approximately 250m along strike and 200m vertically at depth. Resource models for Sariehu UG, Suraw and Obra UG have been completed for further engineering studies. At the Anansu Prospecting Licence, all drill platforms are ready for the commencement of drill testing in Q4 2026.

Corporate Update

During the quarter, David Wiens resigned as Chief Financial Officer, effective August 14, 2026, with Dindiok Chialin, Deputy CFO, appointed Interim CFO (refer to news releases dated July 27, 2026 and August 17, 2026).

Liquidity and Financing Update

As at September 30, 2026, the Company had cash of $64.0 million and a working capital deficiency of $309.7 million. Cash provided from operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $233.4 million, offset by $226.6 million used in investing activities, including $135.3 million of expenditures on mineral properties, $84.4 million of purchases of property, plant and equipment and $7.0 million on exploration and evaluation assets. Cash provided from financing activities was $14.0 million, including $140.1 million of proceeds from private placements, offset by $95.2 million paid to settle price protection agreements and $21.4 million of interest paid.

During the quarter, the Company received the remaining $30.0 million under its $50.0 million gold forward agreement (refer to news release dated August 14, 2026), following novation of the agreement to a third party. The Company’s lenders also agreed to extend the deadline to secure aggregate new funding of at least $100.0 million, initially to September 30, 2026 and subsequently to October 31, 2026, and to extend the deadline for delivery of the cost to complete certificate to March 31, 2027, to extend the deadline for delivery of the updated base case model to December 31, 2026, to permit the funding requirement to be satisfied by gold forward deposits, and to consent to a sixth $100.0 million deposit under the Company’s gold forward agreement with Fujairah Holdings LLC (refer to news releases dated August 24, 2026 and September 30, 2026).

Subsequent to quarter end, the deadline to secure the new funding was further extended to November 30, 2026, and the minimum liquidity requirement for October 2026 was reduced to $20.0 million, which the Company met (refer to news release dated October 30, 2026), and the Company’s senior lenders approved a Technical Action Plan setting out operational improvement initiatives and performance measures for the Bibiani and Chirano mines. Failure to meet the key performance indicators under the Technical Action Plan would result in an event of default under the Company’s senior debt facility. The Company continues to evaluate funding alternatives with its financing partners. These conditions indicate the existence of a material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt on the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern (refer to the Company’s MD&A and condensed interim consolidated financial statements for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026).

2026 Outlook

On August 7, 2026, the Company provided full year 2026 production guidance of 275,000 to 300,000 equivalent ounces at consolidated AISC of $3,200 to $3,600 per ounce. Production for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 165,594 equivalent ounces at consolidated AISC of $4,308 per ounce. As a result of operational underperformance at Bibiani in the third quarter, including lower than planned contractor equipment availability in the Main Pit, reduced plant recovery, power disruptions and a slower than anticipated resettlement program, the Company no longer expects to achieve its 2026 guidance and has withdrawn it.

A second mining contractor has been mobilized to accelerate waste clearance following the January 2026 southeast wall slip in the Main Pit. Remediation is expected to be completed in early December 2026, restoring access to higher grade ore from Q1 2027. In parallel, the Company is implementing measures to improve plant stability and power reliability, including additional backup generation capacity, expected by the end of 2026, and automated restart capabilities.

The Company is finalizing a comprehensive operational turnaround plan for Bibiani and Chirano, which will identify the drivers of underperformance at each operation and set out the remediation steps required, timelines for key milestones and any related capital requirements. The plan will identify the drivers of underperformance at each operation, and set out the remediation steps required, timelines for key milestones and any related capital requirements. It will incorporate the plant remediation and recommissioning work recommended by CFT. Any capital requirements will be considered as part of the Company’s ongoing evaluation of funding alternatives. The Company expects to communicate the turnaround plan to the market in January 2027.

data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- () (BSE: LUC) (Nasdaq FNGM: LUC) PDF Version

Lucara Diamond Corp. ("Lucara" or the "Company") today reports its results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. All amounts are in U.S. dollars unless otherwise noted.

Q3 2026 HIGHLIGHTS

Sales and Financial Results:

  • Revenue was $61.1 million (Q3 2025: $51.2 million) from the sale of 113,227 carats, including the sale of the 1,303 carat Type IIa diamond.
  • Adjusted operating earnings1 were $32.8 million (Q3 2025: $29.2 million). Net income was $6.6 million (Q3 2025: $7.4 million).

Revenue Guidance:

  • The Company increased its 2026 revenue guidance to $140 to $160 million from the previous range of $100 to $130 million, reflecting the contribution from the sale of the Motswedi and 1,303 carat Type IIa diamonds. The recovery of these diamonds continues to underscore the outstanding quality of the Karowe orebody. 

Operations:

  • Karowe processed 829,822 tonnes of ore in Q3 2026 at an average grade of 11.3 carats per hundred tonnes. Q3 2026 covered 97 days (June 26 to September 30) following the transition to calendar-month reporting, compared to 92 days in Q2 2026. On an average daily basis, throughput was the highest in the last five quarters.
  • 94,067 carats were recovered from direct ore feed, plus a further 2,700 carats from processing of historical recovery tailings, for a total of 96,767 carats (Q3 2025: 97,651). 163 Specials2 were recovered from direct ore feed (Q3 2025: 224), including the 1,303 carat Type IIa diamond, a 316 carat diamond and a further seven diamonds between 100 and 200 carats.
  • Operating cost per tonne processed3 guidance for the year is revised to $24.00 to $26.00 from $27.50 to $31.00. Quarterly operating costs per tonne processed decreased to $22.41 (Q3 2025: $25.65), below the revised guidance, due to higher throughput and lower in-pit mining activity, which offset increased power costs.

Karowe Underground Project:

  • The Karowe Underground Project ("UGP") transitioned from shaft construction to underground lateral development during the quarter.
  • The production shaft was handed over to the owner's team in August, and development waste hoisting commenced following the Botswana Department of Mines licensing of the rock winder.
  • Group R Mining ("Group R") commenced underground lateral development, advancing 466 metres ("m") during the quarter.
  • UGP capital expenditures were $40.7 million in Q3 2026. Remaining costs to complete, including contingency, were $245.2 million at September 30, 2026.

  • _________________________________

  • 1 Adjusted operating earnings is a non-IFRS measure. Refer to "Non-IFRS Financial Measures" of the Company's Q3 2026 MD&A for discussion.

  • 2 Specials are defined as stones above 10.8 carats.

  • 3 Operating cost per tonne processed refers to operating cost per tonne of ore processed, a non-IFRS measure. Refer to "Non-IFRS Financial Measures" of the Company's Q3 2026 MD&A for discussion.

Liquidity:

  • Cash and cash equivalents were $232.6 million at September 30, 2026, including $66.2 million held in the Debt Service Retention Account ("DSRA") and a $10.0 million customer security deposit.
  • In September 2026, the Company's $350.0 million senior secured bonds (the "Bonds") were admitted to trading on Euronext ABM (Oslo Børs).

Lucara Botswana management changes:

  • Effective November 30, 2026, Naseem Banu Lahri will conclude her tenure as Managing Director of Lucara Botswana Proprietary Limited ("Lucara Botswana"). Naseem will continue to support Lucara Botswana through the transition period until the end of Q1 2027.

William Lamb, President & CEO commented: "On behalf of Lucara, I would like to thank Naseem for her contributions to Lucara Botswana and her commitment to stakeholder engagement, responsible mining, and the development of relationships with industry and local communities. We wish her all the best in her future endeavors.

Lucara delivered strong results in the third quarter of 2026, highlighted by exceptional diamond recoveries and strong revenue performance, once again demonstrating the quality and value of the Karowe resource. These results, which have led in an increase in the Company's revenue guidance for 2026, reinforce Karowe's position as one of the world's most remarkable diamond mines and its continued ability to produce rare, high-value diamonds. Our strong operational performance reflects the dedication of our team at Karowe and our continued focus on safety, cost discipline, and operational efficiency, which remain critical to maintaining financial resilience and mitigating the impact of sustained weakness in certain sectors of the diamond market.

As we enter the final months of 2026, we are pleased with our performance and the momentum across the business. We continue to make meaningful progress on the UGP, supported by our strengthened financial position following the successful completion of our financing strategy earlier this year. Our priorities remain firmly focused on maintaining operational excellence and advancing the safe and timely delivery of the UGP, positioning Lucara to continue recovering extraordinary diamonds and creating sustainable long-term value for our shareholders and stakeholders."

KAROWE UNDERGROUND PROJECT UPDATE

The UGP is designed to access the highest value portion of the Karowe orebody, with initial planned underground carat production predominantly from EM/PK(S)4. The UGP is expected to extend the mine life to 2038.

On January 30, 2026, the Company announced an update to the UGP schedule and budget (link to news release). Full-scale production from the UGP is anticipated in H1 2028, with a total estimated cost at completion of $779.2 million (including contingency). As at September 30, 2026, remaining costs to complete the UGP, including contingency, were $245.2 million5. Remaining costs to complete reflect current exchange rates and the Company's latest estimates. Committed, not yet incurred, UGP costs were $92.9 million. See "Liquidity and UGP Funding" in the Company's Q3 2026 MD&A for further information on the funding of the UGP.

  • _______________________________

  • 4 EM/PK(S): Eastern magmatic/pyroclastic kimberlite (south).

  • 5 Total estimated cost at completion and remaining costs to complete are presented on a cash basis and represent the expected cash outflows required to complete the UGP. UGP capital expenditures are presented on an accrual basis. The difference between the reduction in remaining costs to complete and UGP capital expenditures for the period reflects the timing of payments, including costs incurred but not yet paid at period end.

Project DevelopmentDuring the quarter, the Company incurred $40.7 million6 in capital expenditures compared to $22.7 million in Q3 2025. Year-to-date capital expenditures totalled $81.8 million compared to $55.5 million in the comparable period of 2025. Expenditures were primarily directed toward shaft equipping, lateral development, including acquisition of the lateral development fleet, and surface infrastructure.

Following completion of the production and ventilation shaft sinking in 2025, the project transitioned from shaft construction to underground development. In July 2026, the Botswana Department of Mines licensed the production shaft auxiliary winder and the man and material winder, enabling lateral development equipment to be deployed underground. In August 2026, the reconfigured production shaft rock winder was licensed, enabling development waste hoisting to begin, and the production shaft was handed over to the owner's team. The ventilation shaft was fully equipped in September 2026 and handed over to the owner's team.

Group R began underground lateral development in August 2026. During the quarter, the primary lateral development fleet, including jumbo drill rigs and load-haul-dump units, and auxiliary equipment were slung down the production shaft to support lateral development. During the quarter, 466 m of lateral development was advanced on the 285, 310 and 335 levels, bringing project-to-date lateral development to 2,121 m. Development rates were slightly lower than planned due to Group R ramp up, the availability of the primary fleet, and by two water intersections encountered during probe drilling, both of which were sealed and grouted. Raiseboring of the 2.1 m diameter muck pass between the 470 and 285 levels was substantially completed in September 2026, well ahead of schedule. Following licensing of the rock winder in August 2026, waste hoisting through the production shaft commenced. In September 2026, 1,603 skips were hoisted, representing approximately 33,663 tonnes of development waste. Installation of the main surface ventilation fans was completed during the quarter with commissioning taking place in September 2026.

The UGP has achieved 2,427 lost-time injury free days. The project-to-date Total Recordable Injury Frequency Rate ("TRIFR") was 0.60, below the project target of 0.90, with a 12-month rolling TRIFR of 0.64.

Upcoming Project Development MilestonesKey activities and milestones planned for Q4 2026 include:

  • Handover of the main surface ventilation fans to the owner's team.
  • Ramp-up of lateral development on the 285, 310, 335 and 470 levels.
  • Completion of the 470-level to 285-level muck pass.
  • Completion of auxiliary fleet slinging and continued delivery of the second phase of the lateral development fleet.
  • Commencement of mass excavation of the underground crusher and conveyor chambers, and continued procurement of structural steel and conveyor components.

Global natural diamond production is forecast to drop below 100 million carats in 2026, down from over 150 million carats less than a decade ago, reflecting the depletion of legacy mines, limited new discoveries, and the suspension or closure of several mines industry-wide. Synthetic diamond wholesale and retail prices have continued to decline through 2026, consistent with continued growth in production capacity.

In the near term, the natural diamond market is showing signs of a price recovery in certain size categories. Larger, rarer and higher-value goods have shown stronger price performance, supported by constrained supply and resilient demand, while smaller commercial categories continue to face pricing pressure from macroeconomic uncertainty and lab-grown substitution. Tightening natural diamond supply and emerging price momentum in larger categories support a more positive outlook for the remainder of 2026.

data.title: The 60/40 Portfolio Is Having a Disappointing Year. Blame Bonds. — Barrons.com
data.description:
This commentary was issued recently by money managers, research firms, and market newsletter writers and has been edited by Barron's.

The 60/40 Underwhelms

AM Charts BMO Nov. 12: Despite the thumping taken by AI stocks in recent weeks, the S&P 500 index is holding on to a year-to-date total return just above 10%, which would be the fourth consecutive year in double digits. Impressive, to say the least.

It's a different story for bonds, where rising yields have kept 10-year Treasury total returns in negative territory, even despite the recent rally.

The combined 60/40 (stock/bond) portfolio is therefore running at just above 5% on the year, which, aside from the two-sided drubbing in 2022 (falling stocks and rising yields), would be the weakest combined performance since 2018. The "balanced portfolio" has clearly been held back by the bond component.

However...one wonders if, with equity valuations looking stretched relative to Treasury yields, especially when the 10-year pushes well above 5%, the utility of the balanced portfolio will become appreciated again as we move deeper into this tightening cycle.

Robert Kavcic

Boffo Business Activity

Chart In Focus McClellan Financial Publications Nov. 12: Different Federal Reserve districts are known for making different contributions to economics. The Atlanta Fed famously runs its GDPNow forecast. The St. Louis Fed runs the FRED database of economic data. And the Dallas Fed has some really interesting datain its monthly survey.

One series stands out as useful for my purposes: The index of Future General Business Activity. It correlates strongly with the stock market, and more importantly, that correlation comes after applying a three-month adjustment. The index gives us a three-month leading indication for what stock-price changes are going to look like.

That is meaningful right now because the latest data for October 2026 show that this index still rising. It's an interesting feature of this relationship that important price tops tend to arise when there is a divergent lower top in this index of Future General Business Activity. Right now, there is no divergence. It says there is no indication of a big, important top coming, at least during the next three months. Some future divergence might develop, but for now the message is that the uptrend in the stock market should continue.

Tom McClellan

Data Centers and Democrats

Policy Pulse Morgan Stanley Wealth Management Nov. 12: Data-center development emerged as a prominent political issue [in the midterms], with candidates opposing expansion winning in Texas, Georgia, and Ohio. Democratic wins in these states raise questions about the durability of political opposition, as well as the timing and scale of the buildout. Geographic concentration makes state policy particularly relevant.

Greater policy scrutiny doesn't imply a lasting reduction in AI investment. However, changes in permitting and infrastructure requirements in a few large markets could affect investment timelines across the industry. We expect state-level decisions to have the most immediate effect on development, while a Democratic Congress and an accommodative administration should constrain sweeping adversarial legislation at the national level. Potential moratoriums in Texas and Ohio could spread spending over a longer period and create room for negotiated infrastructure commitments that smooth economic impact and mitigate the potential of a rapid boom-bust cycle.

In our view, these agreements may ultimately help incentivize more capital expenditures supporting infrastructure needs, although additional obligations could raise costs and pressure margins in the near term.

The recent selloff may create select buying opportunities, where price declines exceed what is warranted by the deterioration in business prospects.

Monica Guerra, Kyle Kerr

Hot Inflation, Higher Rates

Macro Signposts Pimco Nov. 10: October's U.S. consumer-price-index data came in hotter than consensus expectations, delivering another disappointing inflation report for a Federal Reserve that has become increasingly vocal about its focus on price stability. Together with Fed governor Christopher Waller's comments earlier in the day, the report strengthens the case for another interest-rate hike at the Fed's December meeting and raises the possibility of a larger, 50-basis-point (half-percentage-point) move.

Our baseline is not yet a 50-bp hike in December. However, we are shifting our forecast to include 25-bp hikes in both December and January, with some risk of another hike in March.

We would characterize the Fed's current tightening less as the beginning of a new hiking cycle and more as a recalibration of policy aimed at preventing financial conditions from easing in a way that results in a broadening out of inflation from what should have been temporary inflation shocks.

Tiffany Wilding

Jolly Holiday Sales Outlook

Economic Outlook Regions Financial Nov. 9: We look for the 2026 holiday sales season to be better for both consumers and retailers, with our forecast anticipating nominal sales being up 5.1% and real sales being up 3.8%. Barring 2020, when spending was juiced by substantial pandemic-related transfer payments, and 2021, when sharply higher goods prices amplified the boost from still-elevated household cash stashes, our forecast would yield the largest increase in nominal holiday season sales since 2019, while the increase in real sales would match that seen during the 2024 holiday sales season, when falling goods prices lifted real sales.

Richard F. Moody

By Al Root

Ultimately, SpaceX hopes its huge, fully reusable Starship rocket will reshape the global economy, using its low costs to build advanced artificial-intelligence and communications applications in orbit.

But before that happens, Elon Musk's rocket and AI company needs to work out a few kinks. Friday, SpaceX launched Starship, the largest rocket ever built by humans, for the 15th time. Things didn't go exactly as planned, though, and SpaceX shares slipped in after-hours trading.

The launch can be rewatched here.

The test flight, which is ongoing, started with a disappointment. SpaceX aborted plans to catch Starship's booster with "Mechazilla" — essentially the launch tower — with mechanical arms that SpaceX sometimes calls chopsticks. SpaceX will still attempt to catch the upper stage of Starship. That will happen hours from now, after the spacecraft finishes orbiting the Earth.

If the catch happens, it will be SpaceX's first-ever catch of the upper stage.

Catching a rocket is an incredible engineering feat. SpaceX first did it in Oct. 2024 during Starship's fifth test.

Catching aids in rapid reusability. Eventually, SpaceX plans to launch Starship thousands of times a year. Today, SpaceX launches its Falcon 9 partially-reusable rocket hundreds of times a year. (Falcon boosters land on ships and are ferried back to SpaceX facilities.) That's still impressive. SpaceX carries a majority of the world's cargo into orbit.

Starship is much larger than a Falcon 9, and is designed to carry more than five times the mass to orbit, some 100 metric tons, with each launch. SpaceX needs Starship to deploy its AI data center satellites and its next-generation, V3, Starlink satellites.

Starlink is SpaceX's space-based broadband product serving more than 13 million customers in more than 170 countries. The business generated about $3.5 billion in third-quarter earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (Ebitda), up from $1.9 billion in the third quarter of 2025.

SpaceX deployed 26 V3 satellites during test 14, on Sept. 28. Another 26 are about to be deployed on Friday. Those satellites are almost four times the size of V2 satellites, with about 10 times the data transfer capacity.

SpaceX also plans to build the Starmind constellation, which is an AI data center in orbit.

The company hopes to have Starship fully operational by late 2027. Investors will watch that date closely. If it slips, it means slower progress on space-based AI and Starlink.

Coming into Friday's trading, SpaceX stock was a few dollars above its June $135 IPO. Shares have struggled to maintain post-IPO altitude, despite strong earnings, for a few reasons that all boil down to the same thing: slowing AI growth.

Starship might not slake all of investors' fears, but successful test flights can build investor confidence that SpaceX can meet its internal targets and build a competitive advantage above the clouds.

SpaceX shares dropped 0.6%, closing at $139.11 ahead of the launch, while the S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.1%.

Shares were down 1.3% in after-hours trading, falling after missing the booster catch.

data.title: Time for a Grand Bargain on Debt — Barrons.com
data.description:
To the Editor: Jack Hough's debt analysis is admirably honest, but it understates the real constraint: The dollar's reserve status buys time, not political will — and time is the one resource being spent fastest ("The New Congress Must Fix the $40 Trillion Debt — and Soon," Cover Story, Nov. 5). The U.S. can borrow cheaply because global capital values American growth and liquidity, not fiscal virtue. But that advantage isn't unconditional. The danger isn't a sudden bond-vigilante strike; it's a gradual repricing of the haven premium as investors see the threshold for political action rising while the capacity for it falls.

The arithmetic sets the deadline. Political will determines whether we meet it. A grand bargain addressing entitlements, revenue, and spending is the surest way to preserve the buffer we're currently consuming. Inflation, growth, or muddling through cannot substitute for the political choices that will otherwise fall to the next generation that Hough invokes.

Brian J. Gross Austin, Texas

Don't Freak Out

To the Editor: This may be a moment for caution rather than panic ("Everything Is Going Wrong for Chip Stocks. 5 Names at Fire-Sale Prices," Nov. 5). When markets move sharply, it's worth stepping back and recalibrating, but not rushing to the exits.

Data-center projects are already under way around the world. Many have received approvals, and some have everything on order including turbines, etc. Remember, it takes months to build a complete compute warehouse.

Russ Erickson On Barrons.com

Data-Center Plug

To the Editor: As a decades-long Amazon.com shareholder — I bought my first shares in 1999) — a positive article on the company is welcome and, unfortunately, uncommon in the Wall Street press ("Why Amazon and Other AI Data-Center Stocks Will Be Post-Midterm Winners," Tech Trader, Nov. 6).

I must wonder how anyone who has thought about it feels that data centers are bad for the community, state, or country. I understand you don't want a copper smelter or uranium mine in your county, but a data center? That's unbelievable.

Doug Thompson On Barrons.com

Betting on Summit

To the Editor: Great article, thanks ("The U.S. Stocks Quietly Winning the Chinese Drug Boom," Nov. 3). I'll check out Summit Therapeutics and others. It looks like they are conducting trials across U.S. to comply with the Food and Drug Administration. Hopefully, the increased competition will bring down prices for us consumers.

data.title: SpaceX Flight 15 booster diverts to splashdown, missing planned double catch
data.description:
SpaceX’s Super Heavy booster diverted to an ocean splashdown instead of returning for capture by the launch tower’s mechanical arms during Starship Flight 15, according to the live mission update provided for this report. The reason for the aborted capture wasn't immediately clear.

The diversion ends the mission’s prospect of achieving SpaceX’s planned first recovery of both rocket stages using tower catches. The company had intended to catch Super Heavy shortly after launch, followed by the Starship upper stage after a much longer orbital mission. The catches were planned as separate events, roughly a day apart.

The Starship upper stage continued toward its planned orbit, according to the same live update. Its mission objectives include deploying 26 next-generation Starlink V3 internet satellites and attempting its first return to the launch site for a tower catch. Orbital insertion, satellite deployment and upper-stage recovery remained unconfirmed at the stage described here. Space.com

For investors, the booster diversion leaves a key part of SpaceX’s intended operating model undemonstrated on this flight: recovering both stages for reuse. Routine recovery and repeated flights would help establish whether Starship can deliver the lower launch costs and higher flight frequency underpinning its commercial ambitions.

Satellite deployment remains a separate milestone. Completing that objective would advance Starship’s role in expanding SpaceX’s Starlink network, even with the booster catch abandoned.

data.title: Coffee Stain enters into agreement to acquire Chronicles: Medieval IP
data.description:
Coffee Stain Group AB (publ) (“Coffee Stain”) has entered into an agreement to acquire the intellectual property rights and related assets to the game Chronicles: Medieval from the bankruptcy estate of Raw Power Games. The purchase price amounts to DKK 36.75 million in cash and the assets will be acquired by a newly established company, owned 75 per cent by Coffee Stain and 25 per cent by a small group of key members of the game’s original development team.

Raw Power Games, the Copenhagen-based studio behind Chronicles: Medieval, was declared bankrupt on 30 October 2026. The bankruptcy estate subsequently carried out a sale process for the studio’s assets, in which Coffee Stain submitted the winning bid.

“Chronicles: Medieval made a strong impression at its reveal at Summer Game Fest last year. We’re happy to step in and help bring it to the players after the recent developments in Copenhagen. Chronicles: Medieval ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group. Things have been moving fast around this deal, and our short-term focus will be on working out how best to complete the game, together with the new company’s management team,” says Anton Westbergh, CEO of Coffee Stain.

Chronicles: Medieval is a medieval sandbox game in which players build and command armies, fight alongside their troops in large-scale battles and shape their own journey. It has been in development since 2022 and ranks among the top 30 most wishlisted games on Steam as of today. The game’s Steam page currently states a release window of 2027. Further information about the plans for the game, including the release timeline, will be communicated through the game’s own channels in due course.

Transaction and financial impact

Coffee Stain has entered into an investment agreement with the new company, under which Coffee Stain will hold 75 per cent of the shares and fund the full purchase price for the assets, as well as the continued development of the game.

The new company subsequently entered into an asset purchase agreement with the bankruptcy estate, under which it acquires the intellectual property rights to the game and all related assets. The purchase price amounts to DKK 36.75 million in cash, excluding transaction costs.

The new company starts with a limited cost base, which is expected to increase gradually as the studio takes shape. Coffee Stain Group will report on the financial impact in its interim reports.

Completion of the transaction

The transaction will be completed when the purchase price is paid to the bankruptcy estate, which is expected in the coming weeks. Completion is not subject to any other conditions.

Advisors

Plesner Advokatpartnerselskab acted as legal M&A and strategic advisor. Rosengrens law firm (Sweden) and Moalem Weitemeyer (Denmark) acted as legal counsel to Coffee Stain Group in the transaction.

data.title: JPMorgan's Top Credit Cards Executive Is Leaving the Bank — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Rebecca Ungarino

The executive responsible for JPMorgan Chase's vast credit card business, among the largest in the world, is leaving the bank, according to an internal memo viewed by Barron's.

Allison Beer, the CEO of card and connected commerce, "has informed me of her decision to leave the firm for an external opportunity," JPMorgan Co-President Troy Rohrbaugh said in a memo on Friday.

"She and her team have played an important part in moving our card business to where it is today," he said in the memo to employees.

Beer's exit is notable because she is among the most powerful leaders in the credit card industry. JPMorgan's card business is among the world's largest by customer spending and balances. She is leaving for another company at a moment when banks are fiercely competing to win over cardholders, especially those who are higher earners.

Rohrbaugh's team plans to name a new leader for the card and connected commerce businesses in the coming weeks, he wrote. In the meantime, those who reported to Beer will report to Rohrbaugh, who is the CEO of consumer and community banking.

A JPMorgan spokesman declined to specify who will replace Beer. Beer didn't immediately respond to Barron's request for comment.

Beer joined JPMorgan in 2017 as a top payments executive from American Express.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

data.title: First Horizon Bank, Catholic Charities and AltCap Leverage New Markets Tax Credits to Build $25 Million Family Opportunity Center
data.description:
HOUSTON, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- First Horizon Bank () (or "First Horizon") today announced it is working alongside Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston and AltCap to implement an innovative financing solution to build a new 60,000-square-foot facility that will significantly improve access to food and other services for low-income Houstonians. The new Family Opportunity Center in north Houston will leverage New Markets Tax Credits (NMTC) provided by First Horizon Bank and the Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) AltCap.

Slated to open its doors in 2028, the Family Opportunity Center will feature a market-style food pantry, thrift store, and access to the nonprofit's services, including mental health counseling, parenting classes, rental assistance and job readiness resources. It will also provide space for community and first responders during natural disasters, along with ample warehouse space for food storage.

The total investment for the center, located at 9111 Jensen Drive, is $25 million. To date, Catholic Charities has raised $17.5 million in private and foundation gifts. The NMTC represents nearly 10 percent of the total needed.

Congress established the NMTC to encourage private-sector investment in low-income communities, including the future location of the Family Opportunity Center. Under the program, CDFIs such as AltCap are awarded tax credit allocations from the U.S. Department of the Treasury and deploy them to support projects that deliver measurable community benefits. Investors, including financial institutions like First Horizon Bank, receive federal tax credits in exchange for qualified investments. This investment structure enables community-serving projects, such as the Family Opportunity Center, to access favorable financing and move forward when traditional financing alone may be insufficient.

"We are proud to work alongside Catholic Charities and AltCap to provide financing for the Family Opportunity Center," said Yasmin Huebinger, Houston Commercial Banking Leader for First Horizon Bank. "This investment reflects First Horizon's commitment to strengthening the communities we serve, expanding economic opportunities and driving sustainable growth that benefits families and the broader Houston community."

"As Catholic Charities continues its Building to Serve Capital Campaign, the Family Opportunity Center stands as a testament to what can be achieved when nonprofit organizations, community development partners and financial institutions align resources around a shared vision," said Michael D. Hansen, president and CEO of Catholic Charities. "The cooperation among Catholic Charities, AltCap and First Horizon Bank illustrates how innovative financing can help transform lives and strengthen communities across the Houston region."

"As a CDFI that has been helping to increase access to capital for Houston entrepreneurs and small businesses since 2022, AltCap is excited to demonstrate how we can also support high impact community investments like the Family Opportunity Center using the NMTC Program," said Ruben Alonso III, CEO of AltCap. "We look forward to continuing to bring capital and other resources to underserved communities and small businesses throughout Houston as well as Harris County."

The Catholic Charities Family Opportunity Center is AltCap's first NMTC investment in Texas. Since its founding, AltCap has deployed nearly $350 million in capital, from microloans to NMTC financing, to entrepreneurs and communities often overlooked and underserved by traditional financial institutions.
